definition: A privacy service that routes internet traffic through multiple servers to hide users' IP addresses and web browsing activity from websites, ISPs, and other third parties.
metaDescription: Learn about Private Relay, a privacy technology that hides your IP address and browsing activity by routing traffic through multiple servers.
simpleExplanation: Private Relay works like a privacy tunnel for your internet connection. Instead of connecting directly to websites, your traffic goes through multiple secure servers first, making it nearly impossible for anyone to see what sites you visit or your real location.
whyItMatters: Private Relay protects your browsing privacy by preventing websites from tracking your real IP address and location. It also stops your internet service provider from seeing which websites you visit, giving you more control over your digital footprint.
technicalDetail: Private Relay uses a two-hop architecture where traffic is encrypted and routed through two separate servers operated by different entities. The first server sees your IP address but not the destination, while the second server sees the destination but not your original IP address, ensuring no single entity has complete information.

examples.explanation: Apple's service routes Safari traffic through two separate relays - one run by Apple and another by a third-party partner - so neither can see both your identity and browsing destination.
Using Private Relay while shopping prevents e-commerce sites from seeing your real location and potentially showing different prices based on your geographic area.
Private Relay hides your IP address from news sites, preventing them from building detailed profiles of your reading habits and interests for targeted advertising.
